branches.label: Vigilance
branches.tagline: Stay ready, the hour is unknown

branches.label: John's Figures
branches.tagline: Signs spoken in the fourth gospel

parables.title: The Sower
parables.summary: A farmer scatters seed on path, rocky ground, thorns, and good soil, and only the good soil produces a crop. The seed is the word of the kingdom; the soils are the ways hearts receive it. The three failures track the devil, the flesh, and the world: on the path the evil one snatches the word outright, on rocky ground it springs up fast but has no root and wilts under pressure, and among thorns the cares and pull of life choke it out before it bears anything.

parables.title: The Mustard Seed
parables.summary: The smallest of seeds grows into a tree large enough for birds to nest in its branches. A mustard plant does not naturally grow this large — it becomes an unnatural, oversized structure, the same shape the Old Testament gives to a swollen world-empire, like the towering cedar of Assyria or Babylon's great tree that sheltered the nations before it was cut down. The birds that come to nest in it may be the same birds that stole the seed away in the parable of the sower, so the kingdom's outward growth risks sheltering the very corruption it should have kept out.

parables.title: The Leaven
parables.summary: A woman works a small amount of yeast through a large batch of dough until all of it rises. In Jewish tradition leaven was not a picture of quiet growth but a lasting symbol of sin and pride, the very thing swept out of the house at Passover. Here it stands for corruption worked into the whole community over time, a warning that the visible church will never be pure.

parables.title: The Growing Seed
parables.summary: A man scatters seed, then sleeps and rises day after day while it grows on its own — he cannot say how. His only work is the sowing at the start and the reaping at the end; in between, the growth stays hidden and out of his hands. The earth brings it forth in a fixed order, first the blade, then the ear, then the full grain, never all at once. So it is with the kingdom: spiritual growth is gradual and unseen, one stage at a time, not sudden.

parables.title: The Wheat and the Tares
parables.summary: An enemy sows weeds among good wheat, and the farmer lets both grow together until harvest, when the weeds are burned and the wheat is gathered into the barn. The weeds Jesus describes look just like wheat while they are growing — only at harvest, when they turn black, can anyone finally tell them apart. From here on Jesus speaks to the crowds only in parables like this one, because they carry a truth kept hidden since the world began: that Gentiles would become fellow heirs of the same promise, alongside Israel, in the one body of Christ.

parables.title: The Net
parables.summary: A net cast into the sea gathers fish of every kind, and at the shore the good are collected and the bad are thrown away. So it will be at the end of the age. Like the wheat and the tares, this parable is about judgment — the mixed catch is only sorted once it reaches shore, just as good and evil are only separated at the end.

parables.title: The Hidden Treasure
parables.summary: A man finds treasure buried in a field, hides it again, and sells everything he owns to buy that field. The treasure is not a truth worth chasing at great cost — the treasure hidden in the field is us. Jesus is the buyer: he gave up everything and paid with his own blood to purchase the whole field so he could have the treasure inside it.

parables.title: The Pearl of Great Price
parables.summary: A merchant searching for fine pearls finds one of great value and sells all he has to buy it. Unlike other jewels, a pearl is made by a living creature responding to an irritation, and it was prized by Gentiles rather than Jews. It is a fitting picture of the church: something formed through suffering, then set apart as a treasured possession.

parables.title: The Lost Sheep
parables.summary: A shepherd with a hundred sheep leaves the ninety-nine to search for the one that wandered off, and rejoices more over that one than the rest.

parables.title: The Lost Coin
parables.summary: A woman with ten silver coins loses one, sweeps the house until she finds it, and calls her friends together to celebrate.

parables.title: The Prodigal Son
parables.summary: A younger son takes his inheritance, wastes it, and returns home in shame. His father runs to meet him, restores him as a son, and throws a feast.

parables.title: The Unjust Steward
parables.summary: A manager about to lose his job reduces debts owed to his master to secure favor for his future. He is commended for shrewdness, not honesty.

parables.title: The Good Samaritan
parables.summary: A man beaten by robbers is passed by a priest and a Levite, then helped by a Samaritan who bandages his wounds and pays for his care. The neighbor is the one who shows mercy.

parables.title: The Unforgiving Servant
parables.summary: A king forgives a servant an enormous debt, worth something like twelve million dollars in today's terms. That servant then refuses to forgive a fellow servant a debt of only a few dollars by comparison, and is handed over for judgment. The contrast in scale is the point: someone forgiven a debt they could never repay has no excuse for withholding forgiveness over something small.

parables.title: The Two Debtors
parables.summary: A moneylender forgives two debts, one large and one small. Jesus asks which debtor will love him more, and answers his own question: the one forgiven more.

parables.title: The Pharisee and the Tax Collector
parables.summary: A Pharisee prays boasting of his righteousness. A tax collector prays only for mercy. Jesus says the tax collector goes home justified.

parables.title: The Workers in the Vineyard
parables.summary: A landowner hires workers at different hours of the day and pays them all the same wage. The last are treated as generously as the first, and the landowner points out he has done no one wrong — each got exactly what was agreed. None of the workers earned their wage by how long they labored, and the same is true of salvation, which no one earns regardless of how long they have served.

parables.title: The Two Sons
parables.summary: A father asks two sons to work his vineyard. One refuses and later goes, the other agrees and does not. Jesus told this to the religious leaders of his day to make the point that what you eventually do matters more than what you initially say — obedience in the end outweighs a good first answer.

parables.title: The Ten Virgins
parables.summary: Ten bridesmaids wait for a bridegroom. Five bring enough oil for their lamps, five do not, though a lamp's wick can keep burning for a while even without oil, so at first no one can tell the two groups apart. When the groom arrives at midnight, the unprepared are shut out — the oil stands for the Holy Spirit, and looking ready is not the same as actually having him.

parables.title: The Talents
parables.summary: A master entrusts money to three servants before a journey. Two invest and multiply what they were given; one buries his and is condemned, not for losing it, but for playing it safe and never using it at all. Hiding a gift for safekeeping is treated as a failure in itself, since what was entrusted was meant to be risked and put to work, not merely protected.

parables.title: The Minas
parables.summary: A nobleman gives ten servants money to invest while he travels to receive a kingdom. Those who put it to work are rewarded with authority; the fearful servant is not.

parables.title: The Faithful and Wise Servant
parables.summary: A master leaves a servant in charge of his household. The faithful servant is found doing his duty when the master returns, while the wicked one presumes his master is delayed and slacks off. The master's return is deliberately unannounced, so the only right posture is staying ready the whole time he is gone, not guessing at the timing.

parables.title: The Rich Fool
parables.summary: A rich man tears down his barns to build bigger ones, planning years of ease. That night his life is required of him. Storing up for yourself is not the same as being rich toward God.

parables.title: The Wise and Foolish Builders
parables.summary: One builder sets his house on rock, another on sand. The storm comes for both, but only the house on rock stands. The rock is not just good advice — it is Christ himself, and any foundation other than him, however solid it looks, will not hold when the storm comes.

parables.title: The Wicked Tenants
parables.summary: Tenants of a vineyard beat the owner's servants and kill his son to seize the inheritance for themselves. An old vineyard law required the owner to receive some produce every year just to keep his legal claim, so the tenants' refusal was a deliberate grab at ownership, and killing the son was their way to erase the heir and clear it for good. The owner destroys them instead and hands the vineyard to others. The vineyard stands for Israel, and the murdered servants echo the messengers Israel actually rejected — Elijah driven into the wilderness, Isaiah said to be sawn in half, Zechariah stoned at the altar, John the Baptist beheaded.

parables.title: The Wedding Feast
parables.summary: A king prepares a wedding banquet, but the invited guests refuse to come, so he sends his servants into the streets to gather anyone they find, filling the hall. One guest is found not wearing a wedding garment and is cast out — in that culture the host supplied the garments, so refusing it meant showing up in your own clothes instead of what the king provided. The point is that no one stands before God in their own righteousness; only the covering Christ supplies will do.

parables.title: The Sheep and the Goats
parables.summary: The Son of Man separates all nations as a shepherd separates sheep from goats, based on how they treated the hungry, the stranger, and the imprisoned. This judgment is specifically of the nations, distinct from the later judgment of believers' rewards and the later judgment of the unsaved dead — its own event, with its own scope.

parables.title: The Rich Man and Lazarus
parables.summary: A rich man ignores the beggar Lazarus at his gate. After death their situations reverse completely, and a great chasm is fixed between them.

parables.title: The Barren Fig Tree
parables.summary: A fig tree that bears no fruit is given one more year, with extra care, before it is cut down. Patience has a limit tied to fruitfulness.

parables.title: The Persistent Widow
parables.summary: A widow wears down an unjust judge with her persistent pleas for justice until he grants her request. Jesus says God will bring justice to those who cry out to him.

parables.title: The Good Shepherd
parables.summary: Jesus describes himself as the good shepherd who knows his sheep by name and lays down his life for them, unlike a hired hand who flees danger.

parables.title: The True Vine
parables.summary: Jesus is the vine and his followers are the branches. A branch cannot bear fruit apart from the vine, and fruitless branches are cut away.

parables.title: The Grain of Wheat
parables.summary: A grain of wheat stays a single seed unless it falls to the ground and dies; only then does it produce many seeds. Jesus speaks of his own coming death.

parables.title: The Bread of Life
parables.summary: Jesus calls himself the bread of life come down from heaven, greater than the manna in the wilderness, given so that whoever eats it will not go hungry again.

parables.title: The Woman in Childbirth
parables.summary: A woman in labor has pain, but forgets it in her joy once the child is born. Jesus compares this to the disciples' coming grief turning to joy.

parables.title: The Light of the World
parables.summary: Jesus declares himself the light of the world; whoever follows him will not walk in darkness but will have the light of life.
